title: SAML SP-Initiated Web Browser SSO
subtitle: The user starts at the SP, gets bounced to the IdP with an AuthnRequest, and comes back with a signed assertion — step through each hop and learn to read it in the Network tab.

steps.label: Open a protected SP page
steps.lede: The user navigates to a resource the SP protects. Nothing SAML has happened yet — the SP just needs to know who this is.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network tab, enable Preserve log (this flow crosses several redirects and domains and the ACS step navigates away), and keep Disable cache on. Filter on Doc.

steps.label: Request hits the SP with no session
steps.lede: The SP finds no local session, builds an AuthnRequest, and stores the request ID plus a RelayState pointing at where the user was headed.
steps.devtools: Find this 302 to the SP resource. Its Location header points at the IdP and already carries the SAMLRequest and RelayState query params — that is the AuthnRequest leaving the SP.

steps.label: AuthnRequest redirect to the IdP
steps.lede: The browser follows the redirect to the IdP SSO endpoint. On the Redirect binding the AuthnRequest is DEFLATE-compressed, base64-encoded, then URL-encoded into the SAMLRequest parameter.
steps.code:
URL-decode → base64-decode → INFLATE (raw DEFLATE, no zlib header)

<samlp:AuthnRequest
    ID="_synthetic-req-0000000000000000000000001"
    Version="2.0"
    IssueInstant="2026-07-25T15:04:05Z"
    Destination="https://idp.example.net/sso/redirect"
    ProtocolBinding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST"
    AssertionConsumerServiceURL="https://sp.example.com/saml/acs">
  <saml:Issuer>https://sp.example.com/saml/metadata</saml:Issuer>
  <samlp:NameIDPolicy
      Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent" AllowCreate="true"/>
</samlp:AuthnRequest>
steps.devtools: Select the request to /sso/redirect → Headers → Query String Parameters. To read SAMLRequest: URL-decode → base64-decode → INFLATE. Copy the AuthnRequest ID — it comes back as InResponseTo. Recommended: the SAML Tracer or Auth Inspector extension auto-decodes and pretty-prints this for you.

steps.label: IdP login (and MFA)
steps.lede: With no live IdP session the IdP serves its own login page. Credentials go to the IdP's domain, never the SP. With an existing IdP session this step is skipped (seamless SSO).
steps.devtools: You will see the IdP's own HTML on idp.example.net. Under a live IdP session there is no login page at all — the flow jumps straight to the ACS POST.

steps.label: Submit credentials
steps.lede: The user posts username, password, and any MFA to the IdP. The IdP authenticates and establishes its own session cookie.
steps.devtools: This POST is on the IdP domain. RelayState rides along untouched. The response is an HTML page with a self-submitting form — that is the POST-binding delivery of the assertion.

steps.label: Auto-POST the SAMLResponse to the ACS
steps.lede: On success the IdP returns an HTML page whose form auto-submits to the SP's Assertion Consumer Service. On the POST binding the SAMLResponse is base64-only — no DEFLATE.

resp.json:
<html><body onload='document.forms[0].submit()'>
  <form method='POST' action='https://sp.example.com/saml/acs'>
    <input type='hidden' name='SAMLResponse'
      value='U1lOVEhFVElDX1NBTUxSZXNwb25zZV9iYXNlNjRfcGxhY2Vob2xkZXJfQkJC…'/>
    <input type='hidden' name='RelayState'
      value='cmVsYXlzdGF0ZS1zeW50aGV0aWMtL2FwcC9kYXNoYm9hcmQ'/>
  </form>
</body></html>

steps.devtools: The response body is the auto-submit form. Note the action is the SP ACS URL and the hidden SAMLResponse field is base64 (POST binding, no inflate).

steps.label: ACS receives the assertion
steps.lede: The browser POSTs the SAMLResponse to the ACS. The SP verifies the signature, then checks Issuer, Destination, Audience, Conditions, and InResponseTo before trusting a single claim.

jwt.title: Decoded SAML Assertion (XML)
payload: IdP entityID — validate against IdP metadata before trusting anything
The ACS URL this Response is bound to
Must equal the AuthnRequest ID from step 3 — rejects injected/unsolicited responses
Gates acceptance; Responder / AuthnFailed mean reject
Short bearer window; Recipient must equal the ACS URL
Validity bounds — allow small clock skew
Ties to the SSO session — needed later for Single Logout

steps.devtools: Select the POST to /saml/acs → Payload / Form Data. Base64-decode SAMLResponse straight to XML (do NOT inflate — POST binding). Verify InResponseTo equals the step-3 request ID and that Signature checks out against the IdP metadata cert before reading claims (guard against XML Signature Wrapping).

steps.label: SP session created, land on RelayState
steps.lede: The assertion is valid, so the SP maps the NameID to a local user, sets its own session cookie, and redirects the browser to the RelayState target.
steps.devtools: The ACS answers 302 to the RelayState deep link and sets sp_session with HttpOnly; Secure. RelayState is untrusted input — the SP must allow-list it to prevent open redirects.

steps.label: Signed in
steps.lede: The browser follows the redirect with the new SP cookie and the protected page renders. From here on the SP session cookie carries the login; the assertion is spent.
steps.devtools: Nothing further on the wire for sign-in — subsequent requests just carry sp_session. The one-time assertion cannot be replayed: the SP cached its ID until NotOnOrAfter.
